Hi Kenji — good catch, thanks for flagging. Copying Ben who will send a single confirmed invite.

Quick note on what likely happened: some calendar clients (and older Exchange setups) ignore the TZID block in forwarded .ics files and display the UTC-converted timestamp, which can make the event appear on the previous day for Japan. To avoid ambiguity we do two things:

1) Send a dedicated invite that sets the event using the local zone offset in the DTSTART (e.g., 2027-09-07T10:00:00+09:00) so calendar clients can't misinterpret it.
2) Include the local-times in the body of the invite and in the event title (e.g., "Yamato demo — 10:00 JST / 09:00 SGT / 11:00 AEST") and the UTC offset.

Ben — can you send the confirmed ICS and include a short "If this appears on a different date in your calendar, treat the timestamp above as authoritative" line? Also attaching a quick text explainer (timezone-explain.txt) we can forward to customers who hit this.
